purpose: Teach: 白色/股/壺/杭/便器/ふじ/カンガルー/凡人

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが白色のセーターをお着になられた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he wore a white sweater, didn't he?
lines.style: Soft, distant gaze into memory. Long pause before speaking, as if searching for the detail. Gentle wistfulness—not sad, just tender with years. Voice slightly thinner, reaching back.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、ご無理されて股を痛められたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh yes, dear—and when you were young, you hurt your hip trying to do too much, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, familiar tease in her voice. Knowing smile underneath. She's redirecting gently, lovingly—calling attention to his stubbornness with affection, not criticism. Slightly conspiratorial.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが信楽焼の壺を御自ら選ばれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he chose that Shigaraki pottery jar himself, didn't he?
lines.style: Reaching further back, voice quieter. Specific memory surfacing—almost surprised to remember it. Slow, deliberate. The wonder of a small act of care or craftsmanship. Trailing slightly upward with curiosity.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、田の杭を御自ら打たれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh yes, and when you were young, you drove those stakes into the paddy field with your own hands, dear.
lines.style: Knowing, almost singing the words. She's matching his pattern now—calling his own quiet competence back to him. Gentle insistence. A touch of 'I remember you too.' Warm and steady.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが便器の修理も御自らされた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he even fixed the toilet himself, didn't he?
lines.style: Softer here, almost bemused. The memory is smaller now—domestic, humble. A slight catch of appreciation in the voice. Slower pace, as if savoring the ordinariness of it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、富士、つまりふじ山に登られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh yes, and when you were young, you climbed Mount Fuji yourself, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Gentle insistence now, almost lilting. She's building something—a counterpoint. Her voice carries both the past and the present, both his father's quiet competence and his own. Slightly knowing, slightly amused.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが豪州のカンガルー保護区を訪ねられた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he even visited a kangaroo sanctuary in Australia, didn't he?
lines.style: Wonder creeping in now—the memories are getting wider, reaching further. Voice opens slightly. As if he's surprised by his own father's reach, his own reach. Gentle amazement. Slower, savoring each detail.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、「凡人の継続が天才に勝る」と仰ったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh yes, dear—and when you were young, you used to say, "The persistence of the ordinary man surpasses the genius," didn't you?
lines.style: Quiet triumph in her voice—she's been building to this. Not harsh. Loving, even. She's shown him his own mirror. Voice steady, clear, and gentle. The final piece landing softly but decisively.
